messages:
Maya: hey team — spotted a perf regression on /generate over the last 2h, p95 token latency up ~18% on dedicated-gpu-a pool. dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/per-token?route=/generate :eyes:

Raj: do we have a diff or a deploy that lines up with the spike?

Maya: nothing in prod-deploys around the time. but profiler shows kernel selection flip for matmul at seq_len ~96+ -> falling back to matmul_naive instead of matmul_tiled for some shards. excerpt from trace:```kernel_choice: matmul_naive (fallback) seq_len=110 shard=2 throughput=8k tokens/s vs tiled=22k tokens/s```

Eli: hmm that explains extra decode time. any change in batching heuristics?

Maya: yes — batching TTL bumped down by accident in the runtime config (was 25ms, got set to 10ms during a tuning PR). smaller TTL shrank batch sizes and increased overhead per token. also KV cache miss rate jumped: cache_miss_rate: 0.05 -> 0.27 (per-pool metric).

InfraBot: [alert] noisy-neighbor-score high on pool dedicated-gpu-a (score=0.78) — triggered by GPU_mem_churn and schedule_retries spike. See /pools/dedicated-gpu-a/alerts

Zoe: OK actionable list: 1) revert TTL to 25ms on that pool, 2) force kernel selection policy back to prefer matmul_tiled for seq<=256 for model-variant v1.4, 3) kick a KV cache warmup for active routes, 4) add token-level stage timings to per-route KPIs (tokenize/encode/attend/kv-read/decode) so we can alert on stage regressions.

Raj: can we get a quick flamegraph? I'll run a 60s collect on the pool. command:```redwood-profile collect --pool dedicated-gpu-a --route /generate --duration 60 --output /tmp/generate-flame.svg```

Maya: thanks — also noticed an odd pattern: when a particular tenant (client_42) runs long-context jobs, their KV cache footprint grows and causes higher eviction churn, correlating with noisy-neighbor spikes. we should add per-tenant kv-cache-usage to the pool dashboard.

Eli: for dashboards/alerts: propose adding these KPIs per-pool and per-route: [p50/p95 token-latency, stage-breakdown p95, batch-size distribution, kv-cache-miss-rate, pool-headroom % (gpu mem + compute), noisy-neighbor-score]. alert conditions: stage p95 > baseline*1.2 OR pool-headroom < 10% for 5m -> page.

Zoe: I can make the dashboard tiles. recommend a heatmap for mem churn by GPU and a time series for noisy-neighbor-score so SRE can correlate with deploys.

Maya: quick patch we can hotfix: revert TTL + pin kernel policy for v1.4. I'll open a canary rollout to 2/10 nodes first.

sre-oncall: schedule rolling canary, will monitor token-level panels and noisy-neighbor alert. set temp suppression on non-critical alerts for 15m.

Raj: after canary, I'll run the flamegraph and upload. if kernel_tiled fixes it, we should add a unit test in kernel-selector that simulates seq distributions to prevent regressions.

Maya: agreed. follow-ups: Zoe -> dashboard tiles & alert rules, Raj -> flamegraph + unit test PR, Eli -> propose KV eviction thresholds and cache-warming job, Maya -> canary + revert TTL & kernel pin. thanks :thumbsup:

InfraBot: action_log: created issue RED-3142 (investigate token-latency regression + kernel/batching/kv) assigned to Maya, Raj, Zoe, Eli.

sre-oncall: noted — monitoring watch started, ping me if p95 breaches 1.5x baseline.

Maya: will update thread with flamegraph + canary results shortly. :sparkles:
